title: Define explicit core runtime profiles
summary: Add mutually exclusive std and no_std runtime profiles to rumiga-core and enforce their valid and invalid configurations in the canonical host gate.

risk.failure_mode: Feature drift could compile host services into the portable profile or change default desktop behavior.
risk.rollback: Revert the M1-001 core, CI, and documentation commits together to restore the previous unconditional std profile.

compatibility.detail: The default desktop profile is unchanged; consumers disabling default features must now explicitly select no_std, where file tracing is unavailable and blits execute synchronously.

security.detail: No network, credential, authorization, media, or persistence policy changes.

tests.proves: The desktop-compatible runtime profile compiles when selected explicitly.
The allocator-backed core source profile compiles and passes its unit, integration, and golden-vector tests without the std feature.
Both valid profiles pass, neither and both are rejected with stable diagnostics, and the default workspace behavior remains green.
